outcome: Understand what a written text states directly, including words and phrases within it.
Infer implied meanings, attitudes and feelings in fiction and non-fiction.
Pick out information suited to a specific purpose from a text.
Summarise and use material for a context in continuous writing within a word limit.
Recognise how word choice and style create effects on readers.
Recognise and respond to linguistic devices, figurative language and imagery.
Explain how facts, ideas, opinions and bias influence readers.
Analyse, evaluate and develop facts, ideas and opinions using evidence from texts.
Read twentieth and twenty-first century fiction, non-fiction, essays, blogs, reviews, articles and short stories.
Express what is thought, felt and imagined in writing.
Organise and convey facts, ideas and opinions for deliberate effect.
Match register and form to audience and purpose.
Use varied vocabulary and effective sentence structures suited to context.
Write with accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar.
Write descriptions of a person, place or situation that let a reader picture it.
Write a story with a sequence of connected events.
Write discursive, argumentative and persuasive pieces.
Use and evaluate information from texts to write a speech, email, report, letter or article.
Use the conventions of email, letter and report formats.
Use the conventions of article and speech writing.
